{"uri":"tutu://help/overview","mime_type":"text/markdown","content":"# Tutu MCP — обзор и как пользоваться

A search layer over Tutu.ru: hotels + avia / rail / bus / etrain, plus
checkout-link building.
Search + `create_checkout_link` are read-only; `register_checkout_passengers`
is the only WRITE tool (registers a passenger on a cart, returns a pay link —
with the user's consent) — it PLACES an unpaid booking, so use it only on a
user-confirmed flight. For rail, a direct registration additionally needs
confirmed seats and the user's explicit yes to the summary of what will be
written — there is no shortcut around that turn. No payments: the user pays on
the linked page.

## Flow
`search_*` -> (optional `get_offer_details` / `get_rail_seatmap`) ->
`create_checkout_link` as soon as the user commits to an option («беру»,
«самый быстрый», «оформи», «забронируй») — put the returned link in the
same reply. Transport offers deliberately carry no ready checkout link
(etrain's schedule URL is the exception), and a hotel's
`best_offer.checkout_url` is the plain hotel page — the checkout link
comes from the tool.
Legacy aliases: `from_city`/`to_city`, `checkin_date`/`checkout_date`.

## Per-domain playbooks (call the matching tool)
Detailed per-domain fields, edge-cases and presentation rules live in
instruction TOOLS — call the one for your task:
`get_avia_instructions`, `get_rail_instructions`, `get_bus_instructions`,
`get_etrain_instructions`, `get_hotels_instructions`,
`get_multitransport_instructions`.

## Tools
- `search_hotels` / `search_avia` / `search_rail` / `search_bus` /
  `search_etrain` — single-mode search (paginated; transport modes also
  take `sort` and the `price_max` / `direct_only` / `carriers` filters —
  see `meta.carriers_available` before filtering by carrier; `search_rail`
  adds `seat_categories` for сидячий / плацкарт / купе / СВ).
- `search_multitransport` — fan-out across all four transport modes
  (`optimize_for`; `direct_only` / `carriers` apply per-mode).
- `get_offer_details` — full card for a hotel/transport offer.
- `get_rail_seatmap` — per-car seat layout + per-group fare variants
  (refundable / non-refundable) for a rail offer. Pointed seat questions
  go through `task=` (`together` for «места рядом», `far_from_wc`,
  `female`, `summary`) instead of paging the whole map.
- `create_checkout_link` — single checkout handle for ANY offer (pure URL
  builder): a Tutu deeplink that opens the seat-selection page in the user's
  session (avia / rail / bus) — or, for rail/bus with a user-confirmed seat
  choice, mints the cart with those seats pre-selected — a schedule URL
  (etrain), or the pre-filled hotel page (hotels). An avia trip sold as
  SEPARATE TICKETS is more than this tool can put in one link: it answers
  `kind="deeplink_parts"` with one purchase link per ticket in
  `checkout_parts[]`.
- `register_checkout_passengers` — normally the opt-in step after
  `create_checkout_link`'s link (never opened by asking for documents):
  register the user's passenger(s) (passport data, with their consent) on a
  cart and return a `pay_url` the user opens to pay in their own
  session. Flights (`avia_offer`), trains (`rail_offer` + confirmed seats),
  buses (`bus_offer`) and hotels (a room rate's `offerpack_hash`). **A flight
  BOOKS** (a real unpaid order); all of it never charges — not side-effect-free,
  so only on a confirmed offer, and never retry it without asking (a retry
  redoes the work). Read back what you will register — passengers (name,
  birth date, SEX, type, document kind + number, expiry for a foreign
  passport), the trip — from where to where, its date and time, seats/class
  and price; on a train also which seat goes to which passenger, the fare
  and any gender-coupe choice; on a hotel the property and its city, the
  room and rate — and the buyer's name and contact, and wait for an explicit
  yes before the call: the pay
  page shows the personal data masked and cannot be corrected, so this is the
  only chance to catch a typo, and there is no shortcut around it — a message
  that already carries the passport gives you the data, not the confirmation.
  Show the document number IN FULL — masking
  it is only ever a response to the user EXPLICITLY asking you not to repeat
  it, never your own initiative; then name the document by KIND.
- `fetch_resource` — read any `tutu://` resource as a tool call (for
  clients that don't surface resources).

## Resources
- `tutu://geo` — city/point ids. `tutu://amenities/dictionary` — amenity
  code -> label. `tutu://status` — server + upstream health. `tutu://version`,
  `tutu://debug/memory` — diagnostics. `tutu://special-offers` — experimental ideas only.

## Prompts
- `plan_trip` — orchestrates `search_multitransport` + `search_hotels` to
  fit a trip into a budget.

## Output & grounding
The cross-cutting output rules (reviews verbatim, never invent options,
never substitute web/general knowledge, city/airport disambiguation,
emoji, prices, always surface URLs) are in the server `instructions=`
block and in the per-domain playbooks above.

Price basis is declared, never guessed: `meta.pricing.basis` is
`party_total` for avia/bus (the amount already covers everyone searched)
and `per_seat` for rail/etrain (one ticket — a train fare never scales
with the party upstream). On a per-seat page with 2+ travellers quote
`price_party` / `price_party_from` as «от … за N человек», and in
`search_multitransport` compare modes on `price_party` /
`min_price_party`, never on raw `price`.

Places are declared the same way: `meta.from/to` echo `name` + `geo_id`
+ `region`, add `match` + `query` when the resolved name differs from the
wording (`lead` = short form / typo, `qualified`, `prefix`) and
`also_named[]` for same-name places that lost. An ambiguous or unknown
name is refused with `could not resolve …` and the candidates (or a
hotel-index hint), never searched as another city — ask the user or
resend as '<name>, <область>'.

## Out of scope
- Payment (the checkout URL opens the page where the user pays; we don't
  charge).
- Personal accounts and booking history. (Passenger passport data is IN scope via `register_checkout_passengers`, collected with the user's consent.)
- Station-level geo input for rail/etrain/bus («с Казанского вокзала»):
  a station name resolves only when Tutu's index returns the station row
  («Ярославский вокзал»), otherwise — and for bus always — city-level.
  Avia is the exception: `search_avia` accepts a specific airport (name
  or IATA code — «Шереметьево», SVO) and narrows results to it (see
  `get_avia_instructions`)."}
